SourceActivities: 14.3 Turning into Triangles right isosceles and 60 degree equilateral

Task.Prompt: On paper construct right isosceles triangle by 90-degree rotation and equilateral triangle by successive 30-degree rotations. Mark each centre and angle; complete hidden-card rotation information gap with partner.

Criteria.Criterion: states centre, directed angle and rotation direction, and distinguishes fixed centre
constructs two successive 30-degree turns and justifies final equilateral triangle
follows private information-gap card protocol with valid explanation and comparison

Cards.Problem: Find image of P=(2,1) under an unspecified rotation; ask centre, direction and angle.
Cards.Data: Centre O=(0,1); rotation 90 degrees counterclockwise; give details only when asked and why.

Practice.Prompt: Rotate P=(2,1) 120 degrees CCW about O=(2,1). Where does it go?
Practice.Expected: The point at the centre stays fixed (2,1).

Practice.Prompt: Smallest positive central angle carrying vertex A to next vertex B in inscribed equilateral triangle?
Practice.Expected: 120 degrees, since each of 3 equal central arcs is 120 degrees.

Practice.Prompt: Rotate vector (3,0) 90 degrees CCW about origin.
A segment flag rotates from east to north around its base. Describe transformation.
Practice.Expected: Rotation 90 degrees counterclockwise around the common base point.

Practice.Prompt: Does translation followed by reflection always equal reverse order?
Practice.Expected: No; transformations generally do not commute.

Practice.Prompt: Under translation vector (2,1), is image of line AB parallel AB?
Practice.Expected: Yes, or the same line; every point has same displacement.

Practice.Prompt: Rigid transform maps D=(1,2) by a translation (3,-2); determine image.

FirstPartyCooldown: EDULYTIKS_AUTHORED_COOLDOWN: rotate P=(2,1) 90° CCW around O=(0,1), obtain (0,3) and justify equal radii
TeacherReview: Teacher receives separate student/partner responses and marked diagrams, scores 0/1/2 per rubric criterion and signs dated feedback on paper; not a database score.

Cases.CORRECT: 90 degree triangle is right isosceles; two 30 degree turns form 60 degree equilateral triangle
Cases.EQUIVALENT: any translated/rotated figures preserving same centre/directed angle conditions
Cases.WRONG: claim final included angle 30 not 60 or omit centre/direction
Cases.INSUFFICIENT: freehand angle with no tool/angle reason
Cases.MALFORMED: undefined centre or incorrect card disclosures
